newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerian president terms election "a new victory".
newsitem.headline: Algerian president terms election "a new victory".

text.p: President Liamine Zeroual on Sunday termed Algeria's parliamentary election "a new and important victory" for the nation's 29 million people in the face of "savage acts of cowardly terrorism".
In his first speech since last Thursday's ballot in which official figures showed nearly 11 million people, more than 65 percent of the electorate, voted, Zeroual said:
"The success of the legislative elections is unquestionably an additional victory for the Algerian people...
"Our people's determination was reaffirmed again through their mobilisation...despite vain threats and savage acts of cowardly terrorism..."
The poll was Algeria's first general election in more than five years of violence blamed by the authorities on Moslem fundamentalists.

Threats to disrupt the poll, and a call from overseas by the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), led Algerian authorities to deploy an estimated 200,000 security forces to protect the 16.8 million eligible voters.

"The devotion, sacrifices and abnegation of the security forces, headed by the army, enabled the Algerian nation to make its choice in a climate of security and serenity," Zeroual said in his speech reported by the official news agency APS.
There were only a few reports of violence on polling day, none of which was officially confirmed.
This contrasted with the run-up to the poll which was marked by bombs in Algiers and massacres in nearby villages.
An estimated 60,000 people have been killed in the conflict which erupted when the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election dominated by the radical FIS.
Changed rules ensured that no party could use Islam as a political platform in this latest election.
Two legal Islam-oriented parties which were allowed to stand took between them a total of 103 seats.
The biggest party to emerge was the pro-Zeroual National Democratic Rally, formed only two months ago, which won 155 seats.
Zeroual, who was addressing members of a committee responsible for overseeing the election, told them at the presidential palace on Sunday:

"The victory of June 5...is another step on the way to completing the electoral process by the holding of local elections and the election of the Council of the Nation (Upper House of parliament) before the end of this year."
